title: FastAPI: automatic documentation (OpenAPI) and dependency injection

videos.script: Every API needs documentation, and most API documentation is wrong. Somebody wrote it once, and the code moved on. {{wrong}} FastAPI does not ask you to write it. It reads your routes, your type hints and your models, and publishes an OpenAPI schema that is exactly as current as the code. {{schema}} Two pages render it for people. You will look at what they load, and from where, because that matters more than it seems. {{pages}} Then the idea FastAPI is really built on. A route says what it needs, in its signature, and FastAPI builds it. An event looked up by its slug. A page of results. A lock held while you register. {{depends}} A dependency with yield gets two halves. One before your route runs, one after. You will read the server's log and see exactly when each half ran, including when the route fails. {{yield}} And because the route only asks, something else can answer. You replace a dependency in a test, and a route registers somebody for an event that does not exist, and refuses them because it is full.
